Suppose $\log(a)=m$. That means $10^m=a$.

$\begin{align}
\purpleD{10^m}&=\purpleD{a}&\text{Substitute.}\\\\
(10^m)^n &= a^n&\text{Raise to the power of }n\text{.}\\\\
10^{(n\cdot m)} &= a^n&\text{Power property}\\\\
10^{(n\cdot m)} &= 10^{\log\left(a^n\right)}&\text{Use inverse relationship.}\\\\
n\cdot \redE{m} &= \log\left(a^n\right)&\text{Equate exponents.}\\\\
n\cdot \redE{\log\left(a\right)} &= \log\left(a^n\right)&\text{Substitute.}
\end{align}$
